name: PatternFly 6
bestFor: enterprise and hybrid-cloud consoles, admin tools, open-source product UIs
products needing light, dark, high-contrast and brand ('felt') themes from one token set
teams that want framework-agnostic CSS (core) plus React components
complex navigation shells (Masthead, Nav, Page, Sidebar, NotificationDrawer, Wizard)
avoidFor: consumer or marketing pages needing a distinctive voice (reads as Red Hat console)
very small bundles (core CSS is large; tokens number in the thousands)
teams that dislike deep token indirection (5+ hops from component var to hex)

families: body (family-100): 'Red Hat Text', 'RedHatText', Noto Sans Arabic/Hebrew/JP/KR/Malayalam/SC/TC/Thai, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
heading (family-200): 'Red Hat Display', ... same Noto fallbacks
mono (family-300): 'Red Hat Mono', 'RedHatMono', 'Courier New', Courier, monospace
typography.notes: Sizes in rem (0.75-2.25rem). Two line-heights only: heading 1.3, body 1.5 (px values above are derived). Display face for headings, Text face for body: a true optical pairing from one superfamily. Body default is 14px. Global Noto fallbacks give multi-script coverage in the stack itself.

color.model: hex (palette), rgb() with alpha for overlays/glass

semantic.other families: nonstatus (on-blue, on-teal...), severity, favorite, disabled, unread/read

color.darkMode: Class switch .pf-v6-theme-dark on <html> remaps semantic tokens (tokens-dark.scss ~444 overrides). Dark uses #151515 as the page (secondary) and lighter #292929 for primary surfaces and #383838 for floating: surfaces get LIGHTER as they rise. Also .pf-v6-theme-high-contrast (+dark), .pf-v6-theme-felt (Red Hat brand: pill controls, brand accent) and .pf-v6-theme-glass (translucent surfaces, 16px backdrop blur, background image) compose with each other.
color.contrastNotes: Measured: brand #0066cc vs white 5.57:1; text-subtle #4d4d4d vs white 8.45:1; danger #b1380b vs white 6.10:1; dark link #b9dafc / brand #92c5f9 vs #292929 8.02:1. Info is purple not blue, so info never collides with links/brand. Dedicated high-contrast themes exist rather than relying on one palette for all users.

spacing.notes: spacer-100..800 = xs..4xl. Semantic spacers by relationship: control vertical compact/default/spacious 4/8/16; control horizontal 8/16/24; action (button) horizontal compact/default/spacious 16/24/32; gap text-to-element 4 (compact) / 8; control-to-control 4; action-to-action 16; group-to-group vertical 24 (compact 16), horizontal 48 (compact 8); gutter 16; page-chrome inset 24 (glass 16).

radius.rule: Named sharp/tiny/small/medium/large/pill. Actions (buttons) default to PILL; plain (icon) actions and form controls 6px (small); cards/glass panels 16px (medium). Felt theme makes controls pill too.

shadows: directional variants (top/bottom/left/right) exist as separate X/Y tokens
depth.borders: 1px regular, 2px, 3px widths; border-default #e0e0e0; high-contrast themes turn on otherwise transparent borders (border-color-high-contrast).
depth.blur: glass theme only: backdrop blur(16px) on primary surfaces with 60% white

motion.notes: Purpose-named durations: icon short/default/long 50/100/200; fade 100/200/300; slide-in and slide-out 300/400/500. Delays none 0 / short 50 / default 100 / long 7000ms (toast auto-dismiss scale).

modes: spacious (per-component via spacer tokens and modifiers)

components.stateMatrixCompleteness: Very high: semantic tokens enumerate default/hover/clicked/disabled per concept (background-color-action-plain-hover, border-color-brand-clicked), plus read/unread, favourite, severity, on-<colour> text. Count = core CSS component directories in @patternfly/patternfly 6.6.1 (React adds more compositions).

tokenArchitecture: Three layers, generated from Figma variables: palette (--pf-t--color--blue--50, never used directly) -> base (--pf-t--global--spacer--300, --pf-t--global--background--color--100; numeric names, no duplicate values within a concept) -> semantic (--pf-t--global--background--color--primary--default; the layer apps should use). Name schema from docs: --pf-t--[scope]--[component]--[property]--[concept]--[variant]--[state], segments omitted when not applicable. Components then define their own --pf-v6-c-<component>--<Property> CSS vars that point at semantic tokens. Themes are class-scoped re-assignments of the same names (dark, high-contrast, felt, glass, and combinations).
distinctiveness: Composable theme classes (dark x high-contrast x felt x glass) on one token vocabulary; pill-shaped primary buttons in an enterprise system; Red Hat Display/Text optical pairing; relationship-named spacing (gap text-to-element, group-to-group, page-chrome inset); info status in purple; a glass theme with 16px backdrop blur as a supported enterprise option.
weaknesses: Very deep var() chains make debugging and overriding slow
Several doc URLs moved (old /tokens/* paths 404); naming in docs and older third-party write-ups disagree
Warning yellow #ffcc17 is a fill colour only; it cannot carry text on white
takeaways: Three token layers with a hard rule: palette is never referenced by components, base only as a fallback, semantic by default
Name spacing by relationship (text-to-element, control-to-control, action-to-action, group-to-group) with compact/default/spacious variants
Ship accessibility themes (high-contrast, high-contrast-dark) as first-class class switches, composable with brand themes
In dark mode make raised surfaces lighter (page #151515 < card #292929 < floating #383838) instead of relying on shadows
Name durations by purpose (icon/fade/slide-in/slide-out x short/default/long) so components pick intent, not milliseconds
Use a non-blue info colour when blue is the brand/link colour
provenance: public-spec (@patternfly/patternfly@6.6.1 base/patternfly-variables.css and tokens/*.scss resolved by script; component CSS; patternfly.org design-tokens overview); contrast ratios measured by computation
